newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel says EMU point-of-no-return passed.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says EMU point-of-no-return passed.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Monday the point of no return had been passed on the road to European monetary union (EMU), and that EMU would start on time in January 1999.

In an article written for the May edition of the Europaeische Zeitung, Kinkel said Germany had already fulfilled four of the six criteria for joining EMU, but that it must do more to consolidate its budget.

"The EMU is only conceivable as a community of stability. Otherwise it would be all over, as far as acceptance of the Euro by the citizens and above all by financial markets is concerned. That is why the Maastricht criteria cannot be tinkered with," he said.
